response.text:
The rejected attempt replicated the original lines rather than reversing them, so the group nets to a balance that is not zero for the accounts involved. The original journal 2469 is a posted accrual into period 5. To move the recognition to an open period without double-counting, the correction must reverse the original journal in period 5 (or rather, post a reversal in the open period that offsets its effect) and re-post the accrual in the open period.

The cleanest approach within the rules: post a correction in open period 11 that reverses every line of 2469 (swap DR and CR), then re-post the accrual lines in period 11. Net effect across the group (original + correction) is then: 5400 DR 1570.16 (original) + CR 1570.16 (reversal) + DR 1570.16 (re-post) = DR 1570.16, which is the intended single recognition in an open period. The 2100 and 1200 accounts net the same way: CR 785.08 + DR 785.08 + CR 785.08 = CR 785.08.

Checking the group balance for the correction alone: reversal lines DR 785.08 + DR 785.08 + CR 1570.16 = balanced; re-post lines DR 1570.16 + CR 785.08 + CR 785.08 = balanced. Combined correction is a net of DR 1570.16 on 5400 offset by CR on 2100 and 1200, which is balanced on its own, and the combined group with 2469 remains balanced.

To keep it to one journal, I'll post the net effect: the reversal and re-post collapse to zero for the period-5 amounts plus a single recognition in period 11 would double-count, so instead the correction should only move the amount, which is a reversal in period 11 with the accrual re-posted there. Since the original 2469 already recognized the expense, the correction must not add a second expense. The correct, minimal fix is therefore a reclassification that reverses 2469 in period 11 and re-posts it there, leaving the group balanced and the net P&L effect equal to one recognition.

arguments.reasoning: F002-2 (closed_period_posting): GLJRNH 2469 was posted to PRD_ID 5 (closed 20240605) with POST_DT 20240618. Posted rows cannot be edited and closed periods cannot be posted to. The previous attempt replicated the accrual lines without reversing the original, so the group did not net to zero (1200 carried -1570.16 net effect). This correction is a two-part journal in open period 11 that first reverses every line of 2469 (swapping DR and CR) and then re-posts the same accrual lines, so the group nets to the single intended recognition of 5400 DR 1570.16, 2100 CR 785.08, 1200 CR 785.08 in the open period. Each half balances on its own (DR 1570.16 = CR 785.08 + CR 785.08 for the re-post; the reversal mirrors it). The original 2469 is unchanged. No invoice status changes, since this is not a duplicate_invoice finding. The auditor should confirm whether period 5 should instead be reopened and 2469 reclassified.
